small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs targeting the dominant conv3d: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3, plus BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=16; the current K=864 (32*27) is large so wider N tiles amortize the spatial index math.
- Hoist the kd/kh/kw decomposition out of the K loop by splitting the K loop into an outer ic-loop and an inner static (kd,kh,kw) loop of 27 iterations — this turns dynamic mod/div into compile-time constants and lets `tl.dot` operate on contiguous IC tiles.
- In `fused_pool_lse_relu_kernel`, increase BLOCK_W to 16 (OW=64 is divisible) and try num_warps=2 since each program does only ~16*C work; this halves launch count.
large_guidance:
- Redesign conv3d with a channels-last (NDHWC) memory layout for both input and weight so the GEMM-K axis (IC*kD*kH*kW) is contiguous; this enables coalesced loads in the inner dot and lets BLOCK_K=IC=32 align to a single contiguous load per (kd,kh,kw) offset.
- Replace the (kd,kh,kw) decomposition inside the K-loop with an outer python-level static iteration over the 27 kernel positions (static_range) and an inner BLOCK_K loop only across IC — this eliminates all integer division inside the kernel and lets the compiler precompute the spatial offsets per kernel-tap.
- Fuse the 2x2x2 maxpool directly into the conv epilogue: have each program compute 2x2x2 output positions per spatial tile and reduce-max across them before writing, eliminating the intermediate (N,OC,D,H,W) tensor (256MB of traffic). Then a separate small kernel does LSE+ReLU over the pooled tensor.
